objects.description: Enumeration of libzscanner error and warning codes. Negative values indicate errors specific to zone parsing and input handling; ZS_OK is success. Used with zs_strerror and zs_errorname.
Auxiliary structure representing a DNSSEC type bitmap window (RFC4034). Holds up to 32 bytes of bitmap data and its length in bytes.
Auxiliary structure for one APL (Address Prefix List) item (RFC 3123). Stores exclusion flag, address family, and prefix length. Actual address bytes are handled elsewhere.
Auxiliary structure for DNS LOC record components (RFC1876), including latitude/longitude degrees-minutes-seconds parts, altitude, size, horizontal and vertical precision, and sign indicators.
Auxiliary structure for parsing SVCB/HTTPS parameters. Tracks positions of parameter blocks within rdata and the last processed key.
Scanner result state enumeration used by zs_scanner to indicate what was parsed or if an error/EOF/include occurred.

Main context object for libzscanner. Holds Ragel parser state, auxiliary parsing buffers, input/file state, callbacks, error info, and the currently parsed DNS RR fields. Lifecycle managed by zs_init/zs_deinit; used by zs_set_input_*, zs_parse_record, and zs_parse_all.

functions.name: zs_strerror
functions.description: Returns a human-readable error message string for the provided libzscanner error code. Use this to convert an err_codes value (or other negative error codes used by the scanner) into a printable message.
requirements: code should be an error code as defined in enum err_codes (e.g., ZS_OK, ZS_EINVAL, ...), or another code produced by the library
The returned pointer refers to a string owned by the library; lifetime/details are not documented (unknown)

functions.name: zs_errorname
functions.description: Returns the symbolic error code name string for the provided libzscanner error code. Useful for logging or debugging to show the enum-like name instead of a message.
requirements: code should be an error code as defined in enum err_codes
The returned pointer refers to a string owned by the library; lifetime/details are not documented (unknown)

functions.name: zs_init
functions.signature: int zs_init(zs_scanner_t *scanner, const char *origin, const uint16_t rclass, const uint32_t ttl);
functions.description: Initializes a zone scanner context with the initial origin, class, and default TTL. On success the scanner is ready to accept input and parse. If the provided origin is empty, "." is used.
requirements: scanner must be a valid, writable zs_scanner_t pointer
origin may be empty to use "."; exact interpretation of "empty" (NULL vs empty string) is not documented (unknown)
rclass is the zone class value
ttl is the initial TTL value
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; error code is stored in the scanner context (scanner->error)

functions.name: zs_deinit
functions.description: Deinitializes the scanner context and releases any associated resources that the scanner holds.
requirements: scanner must be a zs_scanner_t context (typically previously initialized by zs_init)

functions.name: zs_set_input_string
functions.signature: int zs_set_input_string(zs_scanner_t *scanner, const char *input, size_t size);
functions.description: Configures the scanner to parse the provided in-memory zone data string of the specified size.
requirements: scanner must be a valid, initialized zs_scanner_t pointer
input must point to a buffer containing zone data of at least size bytes
size must be the length of the input buffer to parse
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; error code is stored in the scanner context

functions.name: zs_set_input_file
functions.description: Configures the scanner to parse zone data from a file given by file_name.
requirements: scanner must be a valid, initialized zs_scanner_t pointer
file_name must be a NUL-terminated path string to the file to parse (readability/existence handling is not documented; failures are reported via return value and scanner error)
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; error code is stored in the scanner context

functions.name: zs_set_processing
functions.description: Sets automatic processing callbacks for the scanner. When automatic parsing is used, the record callback is invoked for each successfully parsed record and the error callback is invoked on syntax errors. An arbitrary user data pointer can be stored for later use in callbacks.
requirements: scanner must be a valid, initialized zs_scanner_t pointer
process_record may be NULL
process_error may be NULL
data is an opaque pointer passed to callbacks (stored in scanner->process.data)
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; error code is stored in the scanner context

functions.name: zs_set_processing_comment
functions.description: Sets the comment processing callback for automatic processing. If a comment follows a valid resource record, the comment callback is executed before the record callback. Optional callback data must be set via zs_set_processing.
requirements: scanner must be a valid, initialized zs_scanner_t pointer
process_comment may be NULL
If you need a user data pointer in the callback, set it beforehand via zs_set_processing
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; error code is stored in the scanner context

functions.name: zs_parse_record
functions.description: Parses a single record (or directive/comment) from the currently configured input. After the call, inspect scanner->state to determine the result (e.g., DATA, ERROR, INCLUDE, EOF, STOP) and related output fields in the scanner context.
requirements: scanner must be a valid, initialized zs_scanner_t pointer with input configured via zs_set_input_string or zs_set_input_file
Caller should use scanner->state to drive subsequent processing (e.g., handle include, EOF, or parsed data)
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; error code and other information are stored in the scanner context

functions.name: zs_parse_all
functions.description: Launches automatic parsing over the entire configured input. For each correctly recognized record, the record callback is executed; on syntax errors, the error callback is executed. Parsing stops at end-of-input or if the scanner enters a STOP state.
requirements: scanner must be a valid, initialized zs_scanner_t pointer with input configured and (for automatic processing) callbacks optionally set via zs_set_processing and zs_set_processing_comment
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; error code and other information are stored in the scanner context

data_types.description: A domain name used as the DNS zone origin. Accepts typical DNS owner-name syntax, potentially absolute (ending with a dot) or relative, with labels separated by dots, each label up to 63 octets and total length typically under 255 octets. May also be empty to indicate the root (".").

Plain-text DNS zone file content as defined by RFC 1035 and later extensions. Contains resource records, directives like $ORIGIN and $TTL, comments starting with ';', owner names, TTLs, classes, types, and RDATA in textual form. May include various encodings such as quoted text, escaped characters, integers, base64/hex blobs, and multi-line records.
